prior_decomposition_record.note: never beaten chance at decomposition, to date
prior_decomposition_record.NOT_COMPARABLE: This run's AUCs are NOT comparable to 0.571/0.590. That figure was measured on a word corpus this session never had: food/words does not exist on the PC mirror and no ssh to eran1 was allowed, so proof/make_words.py BUILT one by concatenating dev-split syllable recordings. Concatenated syllables have no coarticulation and no cross-syllable prosody, which makes them an EASIER target than whatever the 0.571 was measured on. Beating 0.5 here is a real result against this run's own nulls and nothing more; it does not retire the historical failure.

words.honest_note: SYNTHETIC WORDS. food/words did not exist on the PC mirror, so these were BUILT by concatenating real DEV-split syllable recordings from food/train (tokens school.py never serves) with a 20 ms crossfade. Constituents are exact by construction. They are NOT naturally spoken words: no coarticulation, no cross-syllable prosody. This is an EASIER test than real speech. The 96 wavs are all distinct, but they are built from only 69 distinct syllable recordings (the dev pool is 1-6 tokens per class), so the effective sample is smaller than the file count.

topography.verdict: a map: neighbours in space are alike
topography.what_this_null_does_and_does_not_show: The placement rule PUTS a newborn near what it resembles, so a positive correlation is expected by construction and the shuffled-positions null will always sit near zero. What the measurement can still show is FAILURE: 192 dimensions do not have to fit into 3, and a rule that destroys the structure while placing greedily would land near the null. Read it as 'the embedding survived', never as 'a map was discovered'. Where positions_backfilled > 0 the coordinates were also assigned from TODAY's vectors (the brain predates positions), i.e. fitted to the same matrix they are scored against — weaker still.
